title: Model chaining profiling and batch shaping playbook
author: Elena Alvarez
content:
Overview

This playbook documents the recommended approach for profiling, benchmarking, and operationalizing multi-model request chains ("model chaining") in the Redwood serving runtime. Model chaining occurs when a single API request triggers sequential or conditional invocations across multiple model variants or pipelines (for example: classifier -> reranker -> generator). These patterns are increasingly common in production flows (routing, tool-calling, multimodal pre- and post-processing) and expose unique scheduling, caching, and batching interactions that require targeted profiling and shaping to meet latency and cost SLOs.

Audience
- Runtime engineers who implement scheduler/kernel changes
- Performance engineers owning microbenchmarks and end-to-end SLOs
- Oncall SREs and platform owners responsible for incident triage
- Solutions engineers validating customer workloads that chain models

Goals
- Provide a repeatable procedure to attribute latency and cost across a chained execution path.
- Offer batch-shaping and warmup recommendations that preserve p95 SLOs while minimizing per-token cost.
- Define benchmark scenarios and acceptance thresholds to gate releases that impact chained workloads.

When to use this playbook
- Adding a new chained pipeline to production
- Observed p95 regressions correlated with multi-model invocations
- Rolling out kernel or scheduler changes that affect batching/eviction logic

Key concepts and terms
- Link: one hop in the chain (e.g., token-classifier).
- Chain: ordered list of links that execute per request.
- Interlink latency: time window between link completion and next link start. Includes network, marshalling, and scheduling delay.
- Batch shaping: runtime techniques to control how requests in a chain are aggregated into kernel batches.
- Prefetch/warmstart: proactive loading of KV cache or kernels prior to link execution to reduce cold latency.

Observability checklist
- Per-link latency histogram (p50/p95/p99) with distinction of kernel vs scheduling vs marshalling time.
- Interlink gap histogram and correlation with kernel admission events.
- Kernel occupancy and batch size distribution per link.
- KV cache hit ratio per model link and warmup success rate.
- Cost per request and per-token cost tagged with chain-id and feature flags.

Suggested metrics (examples)
- chain.request.count (tags: chain_id, customer_tier)
- chain.latency.p95 (tags: chain_id, link_index)
- kernel.batch.size (tags: kernel_variant, link_index)
- kvcache.prefetch.success_rate (tags: chain_id, model)

Profiling procedure (step-by-step)
1) Identify representative chains
   - For the workload under investigation, extract the top 10 chain shapes by request volume and by p95 contribution. Use tracing to enumerate link types and their average token lengths.

2) Baseline capture (shadow/topology snapshot)
   - Capture a 10-minute tracing window in shadow mode with full span collection and kernel annotations. Use the replay harness to export the trace as a synthetic corpus.
   - Command example: 
     ./tools/trace-export --service=ingress --filter=chain_id:checkout_v2 --out=checkout_v2.trace

3) Microprofile each link in isolation
   - Replay links individually against the same model-variant to collect kernel-level latency and batch distributions. Use the microbenchmark agent with kernel annotation turned on.
   - Command example: 
     ./bench/replay --trace=checkout_v2.trace --link=2 --annotate-kernel --concurrency=50 --duration=60s --out=link2-profile.json

4) End-to-end chain replay with controlled shaping knobs
   - Re-run the synthetic chain while toggling shaping knobs: contiguous-batching, interlink-throttle, slot-reservation, kv-prefetch. Capture per-link breakdowns.
   - Command example: 
     ./bench/replay --trace=checkout_v2.trace --shaping='slot_reserve=2;interlink_throttle=50ms;kv_prefetch=on' --duration=600s --out=chain-run-1.json

5) Attribution and root cause analysis
   - For each chain run, compute: per-link kernel median/p95, interlink gap median/p95, batch-size vs latency correlation, and cost per request.
   - If p95 regressions are kernel-localized, open a kernel performance investigation. If regressions are due to interlink scheduling gaps, follow the Scheduler tuning steps below.

Batch shaping strategies (patterns and trade-offs)
- Tight slicing: enforce small, bounded batch slice per link to guarantee lower tail latency at higher per-token cost. Use when tail SLO is high priority.
- Opportunistic coalescing: allow larger batches across links when background load is stable to improve cost efficiency but monitor p95 drift.
- Slot reservation for sequential links: reserve N kernel slots across link boundaries for a chain to prevent preemption and eviction mid-chain. Useful for long KV warmup sequences.
- Interlink throttle: impose a minimal delay between links to allow the scheduler to co-locate subsequent link work into an opportunistic batch. Useful when immediate re-invocation results in wasted small batches.
- Adaptive prefetch: trigger KV/model prefetch for the next link when the probability of continuation exceeds a threshold. Tune by observing prefetch hit success and added upstream latency.

Configuration examples
- YAML example for batch shaper (runtime config):

| key | type | description | example |
|-----|------|-------------|---------|
| shaping.mode | string | One of: tight, opportunistic, reserved | reserved |
| slot_reservations | int | Number of kernel slots to reserve per chain | 2 |
| interlink_throttle_ms | int | Milliseconds to delay between link transitions | 30 |
| kv_prefetch_enabled | bool | Enable prefetching for next-link models | true |
| prefetch_confidence_threshold | float | Trigger threshold (0-1) for prefetch | 0.65 |

Example YAML snippet:

shaping:
  mode: reserved
  slot_reservations: 2
  interlink_throttle_ms: 30
  kv_prefetch_enabled: true
  prefetch_confidence_threshold: 0.65

Kernel scheduling tuning checklist
- Ensure link affinity: tag chains with affinity labels so the scheduler prefers the same GPU/NUMA domain for adjacent links.
- Verify slot-reservation accounting: aggregated reserved slots should not exceed node capacity. The admission controller must expose a rejection metric for reservation overcommit.
- Prioritize prefetch I/O: prefetch requests should be admitted with lower admission latency guarantees to reduce cold-link penalties.
- Backpressure integration: interlink backpressure should surface as a chain-level signal to the admission controller.

Benchmarking suite additions (how to add chain tests)
1) Add synthetic corpus: export representative chain traces (see Baseline capture) to the corpus repo under benchmarks/chains/.
2) Define chain SLO matrix: for each chain define p50/p95/p99 thresholds and cost-per-request gates.
3) Add CI job: a nightly chain-run that executes the chains under variable background noise profiles and validates against the SLO matrix.

Sample SLO matrix (example)
| chain_id | p50 (ms) | p95 (ms) | cost/request (tokens) |
|----------|----------:|---------:|----------------------:|
| checkout_v2 | 60 | 220 | 1.8 |
| multimodal-qa | 120 | 420 | 3.6 |
| routing-fallback | 30 | 150 | 0.6 |

Release gating guidance
- Any change to kernel batching, admission controller, or slot-reservation logic must include a chained-workload benchmark in the release candidate validation matrix.
- Required artifacts: chain-run results (clean vs noisy), annotated traces showing per-link kernel attribution, and cost delta analysis.

Known issues (current)
- CHAIN-2321: Intermittent double-prefetch for conditional chains. Symptom: elevated upstream latency and duplicate KV reads. Mitigation: disable prefetch by setting prefetch_confidence_threshold to 0.9 for affected chain.
- CHAIN-2456: Slot reservation can starve small-batch tails under extreme node pressure. Symptom: increased rejection metric admission.slot_reservation_reject_count. Mitigation: reduce slot_reservations or enable opportunistic mode.
- CHAIN-2510: Tracing overhead at 100% span sampling increases measured interlink gap by ~8–12ms. Symptom: observed increase in chain latencies during full-trace captures. Mitigation: use 10% long-span sampling with synthetic replay for detailed kernel probes.

Runbook: p95 chain latency degradation
1) Triage
   - Check chain.latency.p95 and per-link histograms for the last 30m. Identify whether the p95 shift is isolated to a single link or distributed.
2) If single-link kernel regression
   - Open kernel perf ticket and roll kernel variant to previous stable using the kernel rollback playbook.
3) If interlink gap increase
   - Inspect admission.slot_reservation_reject_count and kernel.batch.size distributions. Temporarily enable reserved mode with slot_reservations=1 for the chain and measure impact.
4) If due to cold KV cache
   - Trigger a controlled warmup using the synthetic replay harness in warmup-only mode: 
     ./bench/replay --trace=checkout_v2.trace --warmup-only --repeat=500
5) Communication
   - Post an incident note on #runtime-alerts and notify owners: runtime-performance@redwood.com. Include the annotated per-link trace and recent commit IDs.

Appendix: quick command reference
- Export chain trace: ./tools/trace-export --service=ingress --filter=chain_id:<chain> --out=<name>.trace
- Microprofile link: ./bench/replay --trace=<trace> --link=<n> --annotate-kernel --concurrency=<n>
- Full chain replay with shaping: ./bench/replay --trace=<trace> --shaping='<k=v;...>' --duration=600s
- Warmup replay: ./bench/replay --trace=<trace> --warmup-only --repeat=<n>
